# ModeOptions

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask docs generate` from `schemas/policy/v1.json`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Mode settings besides the base `mode`. Each is optional in a document.

Appears at: `/policy/mode_options`.

## Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Constraints | Since | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `disconnected_after_secs` | integer | no |  | 60 to 2592000; format `uint32` | 1.0.0 | How long after its last successful check-in a device counts as disconnected, in seconds: 60 to 2592000, and at least the check-in interval. Unset means three check-in intervals. |
| `mode_by_type` | object | no |  | keys: one of `executable`, `library`, `driver`, `script.powershell`, `script.batch`, `script.cmd`, `script.vbscript`, `script.jscript`, `script.wsf`, `script.wsc`, `script.python`, `script.java`, `script.reg`, `script.other`, `installer`, `compiled_html`, `html_application`, `control_panel_applet`, `packaged_app`, `command`, `com_object` | 1.0.0 | The mode per object type, replacing the base mode for that type: for example `script.powershell: audit` while everything else is enforced. `disabled` is not allowed here: only a whole device can be disabled. |
| `mode_disconnected` | [`Mode`](types.md#mode) | no |  |  | 1.0.0 | The base mode while the device is disconnected: `mode` itself or a stricter mode, so losing the server never relaxes a device. It also raises a weaker `mode_by_type`. Unset means the same as `mode`. |

Unknown fields are rejected.
